To: support@clockpoint.example
Replying to: m01
Cc: kevin.mutua@tausifreight.example
Subject: Re: [CP-48213] Overtime coding issue on night shifts

Dear Faith,

Thank you for picking this up. I've copied Kevin Mutua, our payroll officer, who will test any fix or workaround you suggest. Here are the details you asked for:

1. Terminal model and firmware: BX-300. The four terminals at our Embakasi depot auto-updated from 4.1.8 to 4.2.1 on the night of 27 October. Our two Mombasa Road terminals were offline that week, are still on 4.1.8, and are working correctly.

2. Shift template: NIGHT-8 (22:00 to 06:00).

3. Example: Staff ID T-0417 clocked in at 21:54 on 30 October and out at 06:07 on 31 October. The export split this into two lines: 2.1 hrs REG on 30 October and 6.1 hrs OT15 on 31 October. We expected one shift of 8.0 hrs REG plus 0.2 hrs OT15. We round to the nearest tenth of an hour, so the 13 minutes outside the scheduled shift should be OT15. Any shift that crosses midnight is split and coded the same way. This affects 38 night staff, and it pushed our draft October overtime about KES 212,000 too high.

4. Export profile: Payroll CSV v2.

5. First noticed: 5 November, while we were reviewing the draft October overtime. Looking back, the problem starts from about 28 October, which is the day after the update.

The 4.2.1 release notes promised improved midnight rollover handling. In our case it has done the opposite.

We corrected October by hand from the raw punches, but we can't keep doing that. Our November payroll inputs close on Friday 20 November, so we need either a fix or a clear workaround before then.

I also need a plain answer to one question. Can our IT team safely roll the Embakasi terminals back from 4.2.1 to 4.1.8 without losing any punch data, including punches held in the new offline buffer? If it is safe, please tell us whether there are steps we should follow. Should we also turn off auto-update on the Mombasa Road terminals for now?

Kind regards,
Njeri Mwangi
HR Manager, Tausi Freight
